seoTitle: Free JSON to GraphQL Query and Schema Generator
metaDescription: Build a GraphQL query selection set from a sample JSON response, or infer GraphQL SDL types from it. Free, runs entirely in your browser.
intro: Paste a sample JSON response and get a GraphQL query that selects all its fields, or switch to schema mode for type definitions inferred from the same JSON.
why:
When you have a REST payload and want to model it in GraphQL, or you hold a sample response from a GraphQL server and need the query that produced it, writing the nested selection by hand is a chore. The same goes for a first draft of the types.

This tool reads your sample, merges array items to see which fields are optional, and writes either a query or SDL. In schema mode, whole numbers become Int, other numbers Float, and fields that are always present become non-null. It guesses from samples, so inspect the result: an ID field is typed as Int or String, never as ID, and unions and enums need manual work.
howTo: Paste a sample JSON response. A top-level data object is unwrapped for you.
Choose query or schema output, and set the operation or root type name.
Copy the GraphQL text and refine it by hand.

faq.a: Strings become String, whole numbers Int, other numbers Float and booleans Boolean. A key is non-null only if it appears in every array item and is never null in your sample.

faq.q: Does it produce ID types, enums or unions?
faq.a: No. Everything is built from the primitive types, so replace id fields with ID and add enums or unions yourself where the sample cannot tell you.

faq.q: What names do nested types get?
faq.a: The field name in PascalCase, made singular. A posts array gives Post, and a clash with an existing name gets a trailing underscore.

faq.q: Can it handle variables or arguments in queries?
faq.a: No. The query only lists fields from your sample. Add arguments, variables and fragments by hand so that it matches your real schema and the operation you want to run.
